prerequisites: Mathematics: matrix calculation, solving differential equations
Mechanics: statics, dynamics, strength of materials, FEM calculations

learning_outcomes.text: Students have an overview of current methods and guidelines for estimating the service life of constructions. They can select and apply suitable methods for experimental durability determination.
Students can name, classify, and apply simulation algorithms. They are familiar with corresponding software packages and can apply practice-relevant simulation software.
They have learned calculation methods and software packages for service life estimation of constructions that correspond to the state of the art.
They can explain and differentiate simulation algorithms and select them meaningfully for problem-oriented applications. They can evaluate and assess the use of simulation software.
Students can responsibly and professionally interpret complex calculation and simulation results from modern software and use them meaningfully for service life estimation and dynamic simulation.
Students can analyze, evaluate, and optimize constructions based on the current state of the art.
Students can simulate and evaluate the dynamic behavior of complex structures.
Students know the basic theoretical principles and application algorithms to design durable lightweight constructions and they can optimize the dynamic behavior of mechanical structures.

syllabus_topics: Simulation of linear and nonlinear dynamic systems
Application of MKS software to a practical problem, e.g., chassis development
assessment_rules: The portfolio examination totals 100 points, consisting of a one-hour written exam (K1) and two homework assignments (HA). A maximum of 40 points can be achieved with the written exam. A total maximum of 60 points can be achieved with the homework assignments (30 points each).
